text:
anya: Starting a canary bring-up for cedar-lite-13b (int4) — hitting OOMs on our canary hosts when batch=4 and default max_new_tokens=256. Repro steps below.
liam: Ugh, saw something similar on a different model earlier. Any logs?
anya: Pasted the relevant snippet from the runtime:```
E 12:03:21 serve.cpp:cuda_alloc: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation when allocating 1.2G
WARN 12:03:21 kv_cache.cpp:reserve: failed to reserve slot for seq_len=1024, free_slots=2
INFO 12:03:21 request: model cedar-lite-13b int4, batch=4, prompt_len=800, max_new_tokens=256
```
sam: prompt_len 800 + max_new_tokens 256 + batch 4 = big KV working set. We should try reducing max_new_tokens default for canary.
dez: Also check our slot reservation heuristics — int4 can be deceptive with fragmentation; reported free memory doesn't equal contiguous alloc.
anya: Agreed. Quick experiments: lowered max_new_tokens to 128 and batch to 2, canary ran through with no OOM for the same prompt set.
liam: Can we make a defensive runtime change: if predicted working set > threshold, auto-reduce default max_new_tokens or force micro-batch? (cc @infra-bot)
infra-bot: deploy_candidate: automated canary config rollup queued (PR #4123) — will test with max_new_tokens=128 for cedar-lite-13b int4 + soft micro-batching.
eva: Before rolling anything, let's validate quality. Does reducing max_new_tokens change any eval metrics for our summary/regression sets?
sam: Ran quick eval on 200 prompts: BLEU/ROUGE-ish numbers stable for 128 vs 256; only a handful of long-generation cases truncated but recall loss seems acceptable for default. I can attach details to the PR.
dez: On fragmentation: I tried a repro where we allocate then free small pieces, then big KV allocate fails even if free_mem shows enough. Kernel-level compaction would help but heavy. Short term: reserve a small contiguous cushion per process (e.g., 400MB) and prefer smaller slab allocs for KV.
anya: Actionable plan: 1) Roll canary config with default max_new_tokens=128 for cedar-lite-13b int4 + soft micro-batch fallback; 2) Add a runtime guard to detect predicted KV footprint > 80% and warn + auto-fallback to lower max_new_tokens; 3) Instrument per-request predicted contiguous alloc size in tracing for next week.
liam: +1. Also add a test harness that simulates long prompt mixes (prompt_len distribution) so we don't regress.
sam: I'll attach eval diffs and a short note on user-visible truncation. If quality delta < 2% we ship.
eva: Can we also try tiny repacking patch? Even a small trim of KV temp buffers freed earlier might reduce fragmentation.
dez: I have a prototype: kv_trim on GC points that coalesces adjacent free slots; low-risk toggle. I'll push patch behind feature flag.
anya: Timeline: canary config rolling now, runtime guard + metric in next 48h, kv_trim behind flag by end of week. If canary stable for 24h with traffic, we promote.
liam: Nice. One more ask: update the model onboarding checklist to include a fragmentation stress test and a recommended default max_new_tokens that depends on model quant/arch.
anya: Will update checklist and PR text. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: canary_deploy: cedar-lite-13b-int4 config applied to pool canary-3 at 1718123480
anya: canary looked healthy at +5m, no new OOMs reported. Keeping this thread open until 24h mark.
liam: If anything pops, ping me.
anya: Closing note: learned that defaulting to 256 for int4 large models is risky for mixed prompt_len workloads. New default per-model heuristics required.
